learning.learning_goal: Understand that 'how many fewer' asks how many items the smaller group is missing compared with the larger group.
learning.big_idea: Pair the groups. Count the items in the larger group that have no partner. That is how many fewer are in the smaller group.

screens.label: Lesson 002
screens.title: How many fewer?
screens.body: Pair one item from each group. Some items in the larger group will have no partner. Count those items. The answer tells how many fewer are in the smaller group.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Is the smaller amount the answer?
screens.prompt: There are 16 apples and 9 oranges. How many fewer oranges are there than apples?

choices.text: 9, because oranges are the smaller group
7, because 7 apples are left without orange partners
choices.feedback: Pair the 9 oranges with 9 of the 16 apples. Seven apples are left without partners, so there are 7 fewer oranges.

hints: Pair each of the 9 oranges with one of the 16 apples.
After making 9 pairs, 7 apples are left without partners. That means there are 7 fewer oranges.

visual.message: Pair each bottom block with one top block. The shorter bottom row runs out of blocks first.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: What does fewer ask us to find?

visual.message: Six top blocks have no bottom partner. The bottom row would need 6 more blocks to be the same size.

choices.text: How many blocks the shorter row is missing
choices.feedback: Correct. Six top blocks have no bottom partner, so the bottom row has 6 fewer blocks.

hints: Start at the left and pair one top block with one bottom block.
Nine pairs can be made. Six top blocks do not have bottom partners.
The bottom row is missing 6 blocks, so it has 6 fewer.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: What does “how many fewer” mean?

visual.message: Pair the groups. Count how many items the smaller group is missing.

screens.phraseMeaning: Pair the groups. Count what the smaller group is missing.
screens.guidance: The smaller group itself is not the answer. The answer is the number of partners it would need to become equal to the larger group.

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Pair. Count what is missing.
screens.hook: Larger number − smaller number = how many fewer
screens.body: Subtracting counts the items in the larger group that do not have partners in the smaller group.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which equation measures fewer?

visual.message: The gap is still measured from larger to smaller.

choices.feedback: Correct. Pair 9 bottom blocks with 9 of the 15 top blocks. Subtracting 9 from 15 counts the 6 top blocks left without partners.

hints: Start with the 15 blocks in the larger row. Nine receive partners.
Subtract the 9 paired blocks from the 15 larger-row blocks: 15 − 9.

visual.message: The bottom row has 6 fewer blocks.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: How many fewer are in the shorter row?

visual.message: Match eight blocks in each row. The unmatched blocks show how many fewer.

choices.feedback: 14 − 8 = 6, so the shorter row has 6 fewer blocks.

hints: Pair each of the 8 bottom blocks with one top block.
Six top blocks are left without partners. You can calculate 14 − 8 = 6.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Solve without the model.
screens.prompt: A bus has 17 adults and 12 children. How many fewer children are there than adults?
hints: Pair the 12 children with 12 of the 17 adults.
Five adults are left without partners. You can calculate 17 − 12 = 5.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: What does fewer ask you to find?
screens.prompt: Choose the rule that works for a how-many-fewer comparison.

choices.text: Pair the groups and count what the smaller group is missing
choices.feedback: Correct. The unpaired items in the larger group show how many fewer are in the smaller group.

hints: Do not choose the smaller group’s number. Pair the groups first.
Count the items in the larger group that do not receive partners.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Use the idea in a new setting.
screens.prompt: Jamal walked 23 blocks and Priya walked 15 blocks. How many fewer blocks did Priya walk?
hints: Pair Priya’s 15 blocks with 15 of Jamal’s 23 blocks.
Eight of Jamal’s blocks are left. You can calculate 23 − 15 = 8.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: What did you discover?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains the idea.

choices.text: Fewer always means the smaller number is the answer.
Fewer asks how many items the smaller group is missing.

hints: Pair one item from each group until the smaller group runs out.
Count the items left in the larger group. That is how many fewer are in the smaller group.

screens.title: You compared with fewer.
screens.body: You used the same gap idea from a new direction.
